title: Planes Stopped All Over America. Who Will Pay to Fix It?
summary: Last Friday, planes all over the United States stopped flying for more than four hours. It was the longest time all flights had stopped since September 11, 2001. Many flights were canceled, and people waited for hours at airports. By Monday, planes were flying again. But now people are asking a big question: how can we fix the old air traffic control system, and who will pay for it? The government says the trouble started at one small control center in Arkansas. Workers there were changing old copper wires to new fiber wires. A computer part called a router got too many signals at once and stopped working well. The problem may have spread to Texas, too. The boss of transportation, Sean Duffy, says the machines are very old, about 50 years old on average. He wants Congress to give $50 billion to buy new machines. Other leaders say billions of dollars were already given for this job, and they want to know where that money went.
why_it_matters: If planes cannot fly, families cannot visit each other or go on trips.
